title: macOS system extensions, VPN payloads and privacy profiles for Client Connector

prose.text: Beyond the package and its install parameters, depending on the interception mode and features, the guides add configuration profiles that approve Client Connector's network extensions and grant its privacy permissions.

prose.label: Two interception modes.
prose.text: {{interception-modes}} The Workspace ONE guide words the inbound firewall benefit differently {{divergence:trp-inbound-rules-qualifier}}. {{trp-support}}

prose.label: Profiles for Transparent Proxy-based Interception.
prose.text: {{trp-profile}} {{trp-console-steps}} {{stun-bypass}} A machine tunnel in this mode has its own firewall and FileVault prerequisites: [[zpa.machine-tunnels.requirements:transparent-proxy-prereqs]].

prose.label: Private Access VPN for legacy apps.
Full Disk Access.
prose.text: {{fda-dlp}} {{fda-before-dlp}} The macOS versions Endpoint DLP supports are in [[zcc.end-user.service-windows]]. The two vendor guides disagree on one code requirement {{divergence:dlp-agent-code-requirement}}. Whether any other feature needs Full Disk Access is open {{gap:full-disk-access-scope}}.

prose.label: Open points.
prose.text: What happens when the extension is not pre-approved is open {{gap:unapproved-extension}}, and so is profile timing {{gap:profile-timing}}. The firewall's content filter payload is in [[zcc.install.macos-firewall]]; whether anything else registers a content filter is open {{gap:content-filter}}. The Team ID and bundle identifiers are no longer open {{gap:team-and-bundle-ids}}.

interception-modes.statement: Client Connector on macOS intercepts traffic locally either by Route-based Interception or by Transparent Proxy-based Interception. The latter uses the macOS Transparent Network Proxy Extension, through the TRPTunnel network extension (`com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel`), and the vendor lists as benefits no reliance on routing tables, better performance, Z-Tunnel 2.0 compatibility with third-party VPN clients, and no inbound firewall rules unless machine tunnels are used.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector can intercept traffic locally using either Route-based Interception or Transparent Proxy-based Interception.
Transparent Proxy-based Interception uses the macOS Transparent Network Proxy Extension to intercept traffic.
The TRPTunnel Network Extension (com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel) is used for traffic interception and application bypass and has the following benefits:
Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 compatibility with third-party VPN clients
Removes the need for inbound firewall rules if not using machine tunnels
has the following benefits: - No reliance on routing tables - Better performance - Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 compatibility

trp-support.statement: Transparent Proxy-based Interception is supported from Client Connector 4.5.2 on macOS Tahoe 26.2 and later, with exceptions: Private Access VPN for legacy apps needs 4.8, the Client Connector firewall 4.7, the Private Access machine tunnel 4.5.2.372, 4.7.0.380, 4.8.0.281 or 4.10.0.36 and later, and ICMP interception for domain-name-based Private Access apps 4.5.2.355, 4.7.0.351 or 4.8.0.252 and later.

quotes: Transparent Proxy-based Interception is supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2 and later for macOS Tahoe 26.2 and later with the following exceptions:
| Private Access VPN (for Legacy Apps) | Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later |
| Zscaler Client Connector Firewall | Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later |
| Private Access Machine Tunnel | Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.372 and later, 4.7.0.380 and later, 4.8.0.281 and later, and 4.10.0.36 and later |
| ICMP Interception | Supported with domain-name-based Private Access apps on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.355 and later, 4.7.0.351 and later, and 4.8.0.252 and later |

trp-profile.statement: The Transparent Proxy-based configuration profile has a System Extensions payload with Team Identifier `PCBCQZJ7S7` and the extension `com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel`, as a non-removable system extension (macOS Sequoia 15 and later; Allowed on earlier releases), and a VPN payload of connection type Custom SSL with identifier `com.zscaler.zscaler`, provider bundle identifier `com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel`, provider type App-proxy, and users prohibited from disabling on-demand VPN. The vendor also offers it as a preconfigured mobileconfig file.

quotes: Team Identifier: Enter PCBCQZJ7S7.
Non-removable system extensions from UI: Click Add (+) and enter com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel.
The non-removable system extension functionality is supported only on macOS Sequoia (15) and later, so if you are deploying to an earlier version of macOS, select Allowed instead.
Provider Bundle Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel
Provider Type: Select App-proxy.
Select the checkbox for Prohibit users from disabling on-demand VPN settings

trp-console-steps.statement: On the console side, the macOS app profile selects a forwarding profile with Z-Tunnel 2.0, enables Reconnect Tunnel on System Wakeup and, for this mode, Enable Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception; the forwarding profile's Drop IPv6 in Dual Stack Network option should stay off so IPv6 that macOS generates is not discarded.

quotes: Under General, select the forwarding profile you configured in the previous step and enable the Reconnect Tunnel on System Wakeup option.
If you are configuring Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, under Traffic Steering > Advanced, enable the Enable Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception option.
Under Forwarding Profile Action for ZIA, ensure that the Drop IPv6 in Dual Stack Network option is disabled so that IPv6 traffic isn't discarded after it has been generated by macOS
Create a Forwarding Profile and Enable Z-Tunnel 2.0 - Create an App Profile 1. Create a macOS app profile or edit an existing one.

stun-bypass.statement: With Transparent Proxy-based Interception, video and audio UDP streams of collaboration apps that rely on STUN, and STUN itself, should be bypassed through predefined or custom IP-based application bypass or IP exclusions in app profiles; STUN is bypassed by TCP and UDP port 3478.

quotes: bypass video and audio UDP streams from collaboration applications which rely on STUN (e.g., Slack, WebEx) along with STUN using Predefined IP-Based Application Bypass, Custom IP-Based Application Bypass, or IP Exclusions in app profiles.
You can bypass STUN protocol by specifying TCP and UDP port 3478.

legacy-apps-vpn.statement: Private Access VPN for legacy apps uses a separate VPN payload with provider bundle identifier `com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter` and provider type Packet-tunnel; it is supported with Route-based Interception on all supported releases and with Transparent Proxy-based Interception from 4.8.

evidence.after: Step 7: (Optional) Configure a Custom VPN Profile for Private Access VPN (for Legacy Apps)
quotes: This configuration setting is supported with Route-based Traffic Interception on all supported releases of Zscaler Client Connector for macOS and with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for macOS.
Provider Bundle Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter
Provider Type: Select Packet-tunnel.

fda-before-dlp.statement: Endpoint DLP requires Full Disk Access, and the MDM profiles that grant it must be deployed to endpoints before Endpoint DLP is installed; the Workspace ONE guide also says any existing Endpoint DLP MDM profiles must be removed before uploading a new profile.

quotes: Endpoint DLP requires Full Disk Access for proper operation. MDM profiles that grant Full Disk Access must be deployed to endpoints prior to Endpoint DLP installation.
You must remove any existing Endpoint DLP MDM profiles before uploading a new profile.

process-path-versions.statement: With Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, the Workspace ONE guide says process paths can also be used for application identification in the MDM mobileconfig, applying only to Client Connector 4.5.2.121 and later and 4.7.0.87 and later for macOS.

quotes: If you use Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, you can also use process paths for application identification (e.g., /opt/homebrew/Cellar/podman/5.7.0/libexec/podman/gvproxy).
Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.121 and later for macOS and Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7.0.87 and later for macOS.

trp-inbound-rules-qualifier.summary: The Jamf Pro guide says Transparent Proxy-based Interception removes the need for inbound firewall rules if not using machine tunnels; the Workspace ONE UEM macOS guide lists the benefit without the machine-tunnel qualifier.

quotes: Removes the need for inbound firewall rules if not using machine tunnels

positions.says: It removes the need for inbound firewall rules if not using machine tunnels.

quotes: Removes the need for inbound firewall rules

positions.says: It removes the need for inbound firewall rules, with no machine-tunnel qualifier.

trp-inbound-rules-qualifier.impact: Read without the qualifier, the Workspace ONE wording suggests no inbound firewall rules are ever needed; the Jamf Pro wording limits that to deployments without machine tunnels, and the pages do not say whether the omission is intentional.

dlp-agent-code-requirement.impact: A PPPC entry whose code requirement does not match the signed agent does not grant it Full Disk Access, so copying the Intune table may leave Endpoint DLP without the access it needs.

team-and-bundle-ids.title: Team ID and system extension bundle identifiers
team-and-bundle-ids.resolution: The deployment guides give Team ID PCBCQZJ7S7, the TRPTunnel extension com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel and the packet-filter provider com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter (claims trp-profile, legacy-apps-vpn).

full-disk-access-scope.title: Which Client Connector features need Full Disk Access
full-disk-access-scope.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZCC may require Full Disk Access on some macOS versions for endpoint DLP and device posture evaluation, the PPPC identifier is com.zscaler.ZscalerTunnel or similar, and without the profile users on locked-down devices silently lose any feature needing it, or see repeated TCC prompts (microphone, camera, contacts). The guides document Full Disk Access only for Endpoint DLP, with com.zscaler.zdp identifiers (claim fda-dlp); posture and other features are not addressed.
full-disk-access-scope.blocks: deciding whether a non-DLP deployment needs a PPPC profile

unapproved-extension.title: What a Mac does when the Client Connector extension is not pre-approved
unapproved-extension.detail: Unverified legacy statement: without MDM pre-approval macOS asks the user to approve the extension in System Settings, Apple silicon devices may need to be outside a restricted management mode for that, and until approved ZCC cannot tunnel any traffic. The guides give the approval profiles but do not describe the unapproved state. Former zcc-75 asked whether a user's denial of the Network Extension in System Settings > Privacy & Security surfaces a specific Client Connector error code, or an admin-visible alert in the portal or audit log.
unapproved-extension.blocks: diagnosing a Mac where Client Connector installed but tunnels nothing

profile-timing.title: Whether a system extension profile that arrives after the package needs a reboot
profile-timing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the System Extension Policy profile must be deployed before the package; if it arrives after the extension loads macOS may still prompt, and on some macOS versions a reboot is required for the extension to reload cleanly. No captured guide states an ordering requirement.
profile-timing.blocks: ordering MDM profiles and package deployment

content-filter.title: Whether Client Connector registers a network content filter
content-filter.detail: The firewall guide describes a Content Filter payload for Client Connector's macOS firewall, with a socket filter bundle identifier com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter (zcc.install.macos-firewall:content-filter). It says nothing about SSL inspection or traffic interception registering as a content filter, and the deployment guides describe an App-proxy (TRPTunnel) and a Packet-tunnel (pktfilter) provider for those.

quotes: Socket Filter Bundle Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter

content-filter.blocks: building a system extension profile by hand instead of from the vendor mobileconfig
